workaround: Constrain with any or comparable, or use a package-led Go unit or Go island

workaround: Use a package-led Go unit (U01) or a Go island, where struct values and methods work

A package clause starts a whole Go compilation unit; it is not a declaration inside a script
workaround: Start the file with package (a Go unit), or put the program in a .go file, a ~~~go fence or embed go
diagnostic: package must begin a Go compilation unit

reason: Backquotes are shell command substitution at a mixed start site
diagnostic: invalid import statement; use command import

reason: cgo needs a C toolchain and native ABI outside the mixed evaluator
workaround: Put the C source in a ~~~c island, or use a Go unit with a cgo preamble

production: SourceFile led by a package clause (.bsh or stdin)
reason: A file that starts with package runs as an interpreted Go unit: types, methods, interfaces, generics, closures, goroutines. Tour of Go 97/97 and Go by Example 85/85 are measured here
Interpreter-owned values have no native byte layout (operator decision 2026-10-04); existing tested emulation stays, none is added
workaround: Do the reinterpretation in a ~~~go fence or embed go

reason: A compiled worker exposes exported functions through a typed bridge; the nearest go.mod supplies the module
A package main fence is built with the provisioned toolchain and run as a program with the script's streams and arguments
The embedded file is built and run like a package main fence

production: package main fence or embed with an alias
reason: A program is run, not called; it has no functions to expose under an alias
workaround: Drop the alias, or expose functions from a non-main package
diagnostic: package main Go fence runs as a program and cannot have alias

reason: Whole Go source is compiled with the provisioned toolchain from its nearest go.mod; it is not interpreted. An explicit --bashsharp keeps the interpreted route used by the corpus harness

production: A .go file whose package is not main
reason: A library package cannot run as a program
workaround: Expose its exported functions from a ~~~go fence in a .bsh script

production: Go fence or embed without a go.mod
reason: Module context is never discovered from the network or guessed; the nearest go.mod (or a ~~~gomod fence) is required
workaround: Add a go.mod beside the script or a ~~~gomod fence
